title: Residue rank of a local invertible block form
statement: Let Y,Z be schemes [def-pc-scheme], j:Z→Y an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and U⊆Z open. Let M,N be sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with specified finite free bases eM:M≅O_Y^m and eN:N≅O_Y^n [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and φ:M→N. Fix a natural number a and isomorphisms eS:(j* M)|U≅O_U^a⊕O_U^(m-a) and eT:(j* N)|U≅O_U^a⊕O_U^(n-a) [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits, def-weil-additive-category]. Suppose f:O_U^a→O_U^a is invertible, δ:O_U^(m-a)→O_U^(n-a), and (j*φ)|U=eS.hom≫diag(f,δ)≫eT.inv. For any x∈U, the rank of the matrix of φ in eM,eN evaluated in κ_Y(j(x)) [def-weil-matrix-rank, def-weil-residue-field] equals a plus the rank of the matrix of δ evaluated in κ_U(x). No field-valued test point or rank-bound assumption is required.

proof.text: Transport eM and eN first along pullback j and then along restriction to U, using pullbackFreeIso and restrictFreeIso. The local hrestrict calculation follows from restrictFunctorIsoPullback and freeMatrix_pullback. Thus the matrix in these local bases is A mapped along (U.ι ≫ j).appTop. Naturality of Γevaluation identifies its residue evaluation with A evaluated at j(x) and then mapped by the induced residue-field homomorphism. Reindex ULift(Fin k) to Fin k and apply rank_map_field_extension to see that the two ranks agree. This uses actual matrices of global sections and does not require construction of a fibre functor.

Use biprod.isoCoprod and freeSumIso to give free(I ⊕ J) the biproduct coordinates. Compute their effect on ιFree and freeπ by the coproduct and biproduct identities. The normal-form equation then gives the matrix fromBlocks (freeMatrix f) 0 0 (freeMatrix δ) after conjugation by the two local change-of-basis isomorphisms. Prove that conjugation preserves evaluated matrix rank: matrix composition is reverse multiplication, the rank of a product is bounded by the rank of either factor, and the inverse isomorphisms give the reverse inequality. No bound a ≤ m or a ≤ n is needed.

For a block diagonal matrix, the linear equivalences (I ⊕ J → k) ≃ (I → k) × (J → k) identify its linear map with the product of the two block linear maps. Its range is the product of their ranges, so Module.finrank_prod gives rank additivity. Since f is an isomorphism, the matrix of inv f supplies an inverse after evaluation. The identity matrix has rank card I and rank_mul_le_left supplies the lower bound, while rank_le_card_width supplies the upper bound. Hence the first block has rank a and the second has the evaluated rank of δ. Combining the three equalities proves the claim, including a = 0 and empty complementary index sets. An empty U has no x.

lean.statement:
theorem local_block_residue_rank
    {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} {M N : Y.Modules} {m n : ℕ}
    (eM : M ≅ free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin m)))
    (eN : N ≅ free (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin n)))
    (φ : M ⟶ N) (j : Z ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j] (a : ℕ) (U : Z.Opens)
    (eS : ((Modules.pullback j).obj M).restrict U.ι ≅
      free (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) ⊞ free (ULift.{u} (Fin (m - a))))
    (eT : ((Modules.pullback j).obj N).restrict U.ι ≅
      free (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) ⊞ free (ULift.{u} (Fin (n - a))))
    (f : free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) ⟶
      free (ULift.{u} (Fin a))) [IsIso f]
    (δ : free (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin (m - a))) ⟶
      free (ULift.{u} (Fin (n - a))))
    (hform : (restrictFunctor U.ι).map ((Modules.pullback j).map φ) =
      eS.hom ≫ biprod.map f δ ≫ eT.inv)
    (x : U.toScheme) : ((freeMatrix (eM.inv ≫ φ ≫ eN.hom)).map
        (Y.Γevaluation (j.base x.1))).rank =
      a + ((freeMatrix δ).map (U.toScheme.Γevaluation x)).rank
